blind.B1: Yes. GSE60833 (PMC5033478, EpiTrain one-legged endurance training, human vastus lateralis) is an in-vivo exercise series: 68 biopsies. The exercise factor is trained leg (T) vs untrained leg (U) and pre vs post Period 2. Sample ids encode subject+leg+timepoint (T/U x 2/3/4). Paper locator: S2.1.p1, S4.2.p1-p2, S4.10.p1/S7.p1 (GSE60833 listed). T1/T2 (Period 1 trained leg pre/post) are in GSE58608/GSE60590, so Period 1 is not expected here.
blind.B2: Paper comparisons: Period 1 T1 vs T2 (22 individuals, 2,394 genes / 3,404 isoforms); T1 vs U2; T3 vs T4 (previously trained leg, 852 genes, FIG2c n=10) and U3 vs U4 (previously untrained leg, 928 genes, FIG2d n~11); T3 vs U3 (memory, no differing genes); T4 vs U4 (no OPLS difference) (S2.1, S2.4.p1-p2). Groups in this series: U2 21, T3 13, U3 12, T4 10, U4 12.
blind.B3: Yes, repeated measures: every subject gives both legs and up to 4 time points (S2.1.p1, S4.2). Unit = subject, parsed from the 'original sample id' (e.g. 12T3 -> subject 12); the metadata also holds a subject-like field. Packet A's title-suffix pairing keys link 0/68 samples, so the subject must come from the original sample id.
blind.B4: The paper fits each pair of groups alone: separate OPLS/PCA models per comparison (T1 vs T2, T3 vs T4, U3 vs U4, T3 vs U3, T4 vs U4; S2.1.p2-p3, S2.4, S4.6.p1 'comparing leg biopsies collected before and after'). It does not state a single joint model. Univariate limma is mentioned for HTSeq counts (S4.5.p1) and novel transcripts (S2.3.p1).
blind.B5: Gene/isoform DEG rule: OPLS loading significance, ABS(loading) - ABS(jack-knife confidence interval) > 0 at 99% confidence, Simca significance level 0.01, on ComBat-batch-corrected FPKM with mean FPKM > 1; no fold-change cutoff (S4.6.p1-p2, S2.1.p2). Counts: Period 1 2,394 genes / 3,404 isoforms; T3 vs T4 852 genes; U3 vs U4 928 genes; 180 shared (S2.4.p2); T3 vs U3 none (S2.4.p1); 12,848 genes entered (S4.6.p1). Limma novel-transcript rule: adj p <= 0.05 (Table 3).

checks.evidence: Series run for the exercise question; matches B1 (trained vs untrained leg, pre/post training). Period 1 stated as out of scope for this accession in paper_data_discrepancies (T1/T2 in GSE58608/GSE60590).

grp from original sample id: U2 21, T3 13, T4 10, U3 12, U4 12 = 68 (packet A). Control is T3 for T4 and U3 for U4 (own-leg pre-training baseline, S2.4.p2). The metadata 'exercise status' column is rejected with a reason. Per-contrast dropping of unpaired subjects (20 of 23 T3/T4 samples, 22 of 24 U3/U4) is shown as complete-pair counts (10 and 11), which match FIG2c/d n.
Contrasts are T4 (treatment) vs T3 (control) and U4 vs U3; leg comparisons T3 vs U3 and T4 vs U4 are exploratory. GSEA OXPHOS is positive (NES 3.69/3.16) as expected for post-training.
Design ~ subject + grp with subject recoded to S<n> (categorical, not a slope), full rank 27, residual df 41; blocking_terms=[subject]; per-contrast fits use complete pairs.

One fit per contrast on only the two groups involved, as the paper fitted each pair alone (B4). The packet B suitability line about omitting sex/location (rank deficient) is consistent with subject blocking.

Sequencing batch is not in GEO (the paper used ComBat) and the case records it as a caveat. Sex and biopsy side are constant within subject-leg and absorbed by subject blocking. Minor: the study caveat attributes the excess of nominal p<0.05 genes in T3 vs U3 (1784/13035) to 'unmodelled sequencing batch' without data support; that is a hypothesis, not a finding.
checks.fix: Reword the caveat to 'possibly unmodelled batch'.

checks.evidence: Cufflinks FPKM (non-integer, integer_fraction 0.584, max 87763), limma on log2(FPKM+1) with mean FPKM >= 1 filter; the paper's gene-level input was also (ComBat) FPKM. p-value histogram sane: frac_p>0.9 about 0.07, frac_p<0.05 0.11-0.14; no TMM/voom issue.

Paper rule is OPLS loading minus jack-knife CI > 0 (S4.6.p2), not convertible; the case records the deviation (threshold_source workflow_default, padj < 0.05, no FC) with an audit rule p < 0.01 and the deviation_note. No tested rule reproduces the paper's 852/928 (padj<0.1: 1472/1808; p<0.01: 409/646; p<0.05: 101/98 appear in the table, with only p<0.01 / padj<0.1 of similar order), and the case does not claim a match.

Paper counts are taken from the same contrasts (852 for T3 vs T4, 928 for U3 vs U4, 0 for T3 vs U3). HANDBACK states 0/6 vs 852/928 openly, calls counts not comparable and claims agreement only on direction of named genes and OXPHOS, which the GSEA supports.

No stopped case. The OPLS paper route is blocked because Simca has no executor and ComBat batch labels are absent from GEO (true: batch labels not in metadata constant/per-sample columns). ORA for T4 vs T3 not run because 0 genes pass padj<0.05 (true). Period 1 not analysed because T1/T2 are in other accessions (S4.10.p1).

human_items: Open policy: which threshold to report when the paper's rule (OPLS loadings) has no p-value equivalent and the headline counts (852/928) are far above what BH padj < 0.05 gives (0/6); the case's choice (padj 0.05 applied, p<0.01 audit) is recorded and labelled, so it is not an error.
Open policy: the paper's headline result needs T1/T2 from GSE58608/GSE60590; whether a joint multi-accession analysis should be queued is a scoping decision for the person.
summary: 该案例通过：处理的是论文的第二训练期（T3 vs T4、U3 vs U4）及腿间探索性比较，方向、对照、按受试者配对（~ subject + grp，满秩）和逐对拟合都与论文一致。论文的 OPLS 判定规则无法转换为 p 值，案例已如实记录为偏离并给出审计阈值，且没有声称与论文的 852/928 一致；仅有批次来源的措辞为次要问题。
